text: This capstone follows Mara Voss, a Security Engineer at Hartwell Regional Utilities, a regional electric and water utility. It picks up right after the Intermediate project's incident, where Mara traced a 3 a.m. alert back to an overly broad firewall rule nobody had flagged.

That fixed rule didn't stay a closed ticket. It escalated into a full board-level security review, commissioned by Hartwell's CISO, Howard Okonjo. The board's question was blunt: if that rule sat undetected that long, what else looks like it, especially in Hartwell's OT and SCADA systems that run actual substations and water treatment?

The review produced four funded workstreams: a zero-trust network segmentation pilot, one consolidated view of identity across Azure AD and AWS IAM, Python-based security automation to replace manual access reviews, and a formal GRC risk register to track every finding. The board approved $340,000 for Phase 1 and gave the program 90 days to deliver a working pilot and report back.

Mara has also been promoted to Security Engineer, which means designing and building these controls, not just operating and triaging them. Next lesson scopes exactly which network boundary this pilot will target first.
